skill.name: discord-automation
skill.description: Guide Discord automation through Rube MCP for messages, DMs, roles, webhooks, reactions, and permission-aware workflows.
skill.summary: Guide permission-aware Discord automation through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code in a documentation-only skill. The remaining risks are the intended external Rube MCP connection and Discord workflows that can send messages, manage roles, manage webhooks, and delete reactions when authorized.

remediation.suggestion: Document the Rube MCP trust boundary, what Discord data can be accessed, and when users must approve the OAuth or bot connection.
Require explicit confirmation before role changes, member updates, webhook changes, reaction deletion, or any operation with broad server impact.
Add safeguards for message previews, recipient confirmation, rate-limit handling, and policy compliance before sending DMs, channel posts, or webhook messages.

remediation.issue: Markdown inline code triggered static command findings
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that listed tool names and parameters are Rube MCP identifiers, not shell commands, to reduce scanner ambiguity.

- Reactions: max 100 per request, use `after` for pagination
- `discordbot` toolkit uses bot tokens; `discord` uses user OAuth

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Discord Administration Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill guides role creation, role assignment, role deletion, member updates, webhook creation, webhook execution, and reaction deletion. These actions can alter server access or content when used with broad bot permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections explicitly document role, member, webhook, and reaction management workflows, including destructive deletion and permission requirements. The risk is contextual and depends on the connected Discord account or bot authority.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Messaging and Webhook Abuse Potential
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports channel messages, direct messages, and webhook messages with custom sender presentation. Without user approval and rate-limit controls, these workflows can send unwanted messages or impersonate integrations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections describe message sending, DM creation, webhook execution, and custom webhook identity. The skill also notes rate limits, so the abuse concern is clear but bounded by Discord permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party MCP Authorization Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The setup asks users to add the Rube MCP endpoint and complete Discord authorization through the returned link. Users must trust that external MCP service with the Discord actions available to the connected account or bot.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup and token sections explicitly describe adding an external MCP endpoint and using bot or user OAuth connections. This does not prove malicious behavior, but it is a real authorization and trust boundary.

content.user_title: Automate Discord Workflows with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Discord automation often requires many tool calls, permissions, and IDs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for messages, roles, webhooks, and reactions.
actual_capabilities: Guides assistants to search Rube MCP for current Discord and Discordbot tool schemas.
Helps send channel messages and direct messages after channel or recipient IDs are known.
Documents role creation, role assignment, role deletion, and member update workflows.
Supports webhook listing, creation, execution, and update workflows through Discordbot tools.
Covers reaction listing and reaction removal workflows with required message and emoji IDs.
Explains Discord snowflake IDs, permission bitfields, pagination, and rate-limit handling.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP to be connected and available in the client.
Requires an active Discord or Discordbot connection with valid permissions.
Cannot bypass Discord API permissions, rate limits, or platform policies.
Destructive actions still need human review and environment-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Post Server Announcements
use_cases.description: Prepare and send approved announcements to selected Discord channels with the correct guild and channel IDs.

use_cases.title: Maintain Member Roles
use_cases.description: Create, assign, remove, or inspect roles while checking hierarchy and permission limits before each action.

use_cases.title: Connect External Alerts
use_cases.description: Create and execute webhooks for approved integrations that publish operational updates into Discord channels.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Channel Message
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a single approved message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Discord automation skill to send an approved message to a Discord channel. Search Rube MCP for current Discordbot message tools first. Ask me for missing guild or channel IDs before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Create and Assign a Role
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for member access changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Discord automation skill to create a role and assign it to selected members. Confirm the guild ID, role name, permission bitfield, member IDs, and bot role hierarchy first.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Webhook Alert
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Discord automation skill to create a webhook for an approved alert channel. Search for latest webhook schemas. Confirm the channel ID and webhook name. Prepare a test message for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Discord Workflow Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for safe multi-step automation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Discord automation skill to plan a multi-step workflow for messages, roles, and reactions. List each Rube MCP tool call, required ID, permission check, confirmation point, and rollback option before execution.

output_examples.input: Send a launch announcement to our community updates channel.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the needed guild and channel, previews the announcement, confirms permissions, and sends the message only after approval.

output_examples.input: Give three members the event volunteer role.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the guild, member IDs, target role, and role hierarchy, then applies the role assignments and reports the result.

output_examples.input: Create a webhook for deployment alerts.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the target channel, creates the webhook with an approved name, sends a test alert, and reminds the user to protect the token.

best_practices: Search Rube MCP for current tool schemas before choosing a Discord or Discordbot tool.
Confirm guild, channel, user, role, message, and webhook IDs before executing actions.
Preview outbound messages and require approval for DMs, webhooks, role changes, and deletions.
anti_patterns: Do not send bulk DMs or announcements without explicit recipient and content approval.
Do not use administrator permissions when a narrower Discord permission is enough.
Do not store or expose webhook tokens, OAuth links, or Discord identifiers in shared outputs.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable code?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill that guides Rube MCP tool selection and Discord workflow sequencing.

faq.question: What must be connected before using it?
faq.answer: Rube MCP must be available, and Discord or Discordbot must have an active authorized connection.

faq.question: Can it send messages automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide message sending through Discordbot tools, but users should approve recipients and content first.

faq.question: Can it manage Discord roles?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents role creation, assignment, deletion, and member update workflows when the bot has permission.

faq.question: How does it handle changing tool schemas?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS first so current schemas are used.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are third-party MCP authorization, privileged Discord actions, webhook tokens, and unwanted messages.
